repo.description:
## What happened

`user.update` lets a user edit their profile, but the update schema is `createSchema.partial()` (`db/schema/user.ts:235`), so every column on the user table is writable, and the router passes the input straight to `updateUser(ctx.user.id, input)` (`routers/user.ts:273`).

Confirmed on dokploy.com: one request set `serversQuantity` to 999 on my own account (reverted afterwards). Fields that should be server-managed are client-writable, including:

- `serversQuantity`: bypasses the plan limit on how many servers you can add
- `expirationDate`: self-extend a trial/subscription
- `banned`: self-unban
- `enablePaidFeatures` / `enableEnterpriseFeatures`: flip feature flags
- `emailVerified`, `stripeCustomerId`, `licenseKey`, `allowImpersonation`, ...

The `role` and `isValidEnterpriseLicense` fields are correctly omitted, so this is not a direct privilege escalation.

The `stripeCustomerId` field makes this more serious. It is the key used to resolve a user's billing identity:

- `getCurrentPlanForUser` (`server/utils/billing.ts:48`) lists active Stripe subscriptions for `customer: stripeCustomerId` on every plan check. Set your account's `stripeCustomerId` to a paying customer's `cus_...`, and your organization resolves to their plan: unlimited servers, unlimited members, no payment.
- Billing-portal sessions are created for that same customer ID, so a spoofed account gets a portal into the victim's Stripe customer: invoices, billing details, payment-method metadata, cancel/modify the subscription.
- Stripe webhooks match users by `stripeCustomerId` (`pages/api/stripe/webhook.ts`), so subscription updates get credited to the wrong account.

Requires knowing the victim's `cus_...` ID (leaks via invoices, emails, support threads). Still worth locking down: it converts a self-scoped field bug into cross-customer billing access.

## How to reproduce

```js
fetch("/api/trpc/user.update?batch=1", {
  method: "POST", credentials: "include",
  headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ "0": { "json": { "serversQuantity": 999 } } })
})
```

## Suggested fix

Replace `createSchema.partial()` with an explicit `.pick()` of the fields a user may edit (name, email, password, avatar, notification prefs, ...). This is the same pattern as the `project.update` issue reported separately (GHSA-h52x-gwf8-4h58); worth auditing every `*.partial()` update schema for columns that must be immutable.
repo.summary: Users can overwrite server-managed fields on their own account via `user.update`
